newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police officer admits tipping off dealer.
newsitem.headline: French police officer admits tipping off dealer.

text.p: One of France's top police detectives admitted in court on Monday tipping off a drugs trafficker about a police probe but denied any knowledge of his friend's illegal dealings.
Philippe Feval, deputy head of a police unit specialised in cracking down on major gangland activity, was sentenced to four years in jail last year for complicity in drugs running.

Feval acknowledged that he was a friend of restaurant owner Roland Plegat, a drugs trafficker sentenced to 20 years imprisonment, and that he told him that a separate anti-drugs unit was watching him.

"I didn't think the case was that serious. If I'd known there was a judicial investigation under way, I wouldn't have behaved that way," Feval, who was regularly offered free meals by Plegat, told the court.

In July 1992, Feval and his men tailed two individuals whom Plegat had told them about. The restaurant owner said they had approached him to suggest a drug deal. Feval eventually found out that the two men were part of the anti-drugs unit.
"I wanted to cover my department's blunder, that surveillance. I didn't think that Plegat could be mixed up in drugs," Feval said.
Feval's deputy Thierry Dentz was last year sentenced to three years imprisonment.
